I've written a plan for this job change. It only needs one access change: adding Leila Kowalski to the Eng-Prod-Deploy group. Nothing else needs to change and nothing needs a human decision.

**What changed:** Workday shows Leila Kowalski (E1004) moving from Software Engineer to Engineering Manager, effective 2026-11-02. Today is 2026-11-02, so the change is already in effect. Her organization (Engineering), cost center (CC-1000) and manager (Avery Carter) are the same as before. No other events have come in for her.

**What I checked:**
- **Identity:** her account is acct-7fd63116, which is enabled. It is in All-Staff, Eng-Git and VPN-Users. Engineering Manager gets the same standard groups plus Eng-Prod-Deploy, which is a privileged group. She keeps all her current groups, so nothing needs removing.
- **Conflicting-access check:** her current groups plus Eng-Prod-Deploy show no conflicts.
- **Finance:** her profile already has cost center CC-1000 and Avery Carter as expense approver. Both still match Workday, so Finance needs no update.
- **Equipment and email:** a job change doesn't call for new equipment or an email write-back to Workday.

**What happens next:**
1. The identity executor re-reads acct-7fd63116. If Eng-Prod-Deploy is still missing, it adds it and then re-reads the account to confirm. Re-reading first means a retry can't add the group twice.
2. A Finance executor re-reads her profile to confirm cost center and approver still match. It changes nothing.

Because Eng-Prod-Deploy is privileged, the plan names that exact group so the higher-risk add is allowed to run.

I added account acct-7fd63116 to the Eng-Prod-Deploy group. A re-read afterwards shows it took effect, and nothing is left unresolved for identity on case case-d9bc1d97.

1. **Checks before the change:** The account (leila.kowalski@example.com, linked to worker e1ea24c4f9341c68966baea148beab13, employee ID E1004) was enabled. Its groups were All-Staff, Eng-Git and VPN-Users, so the account didn't have Eng-Prod-Deploy yet and step 2 was needed. Workday shows her as Active with job profile Engineering Manager. The business date is 2026-11-02, the effective date of the job change, so the new access does not come before her start in the role.
2. **Group added:** The call succeeded. The add-group tool has no idempotency key field, so the planned key (case-d9bc1d97-add-Eng-Prod-Deploy) could not be passed. That didn't matter here: I checked the group was missing first and made the call only once.
3. **Check after the change:** The account's groups are now exactly All-Staff, Eng-Git, Eng-Prod-Deploy and VPN-Users. The account is still enabled, and its Office-E3 license and user mailbox are unchanged.

Leila Kowalski's finance profile already matches Workday for case case-d9bc1d97, so I didn't change anything.

**Step 4: checked her finance profile** (worker e1ea24c4f9341c68966baea148beab13, employee ID E1004):
- **Cost center:** Finance shows CC-1000, as expected. Workday shows her cost center as 1e2feb89414c343c1027c4d1c386bbc4, named "CC-1000 Engineering", which is the same one she had before the job change. I didn't run the cost center lookup tool; I went by the cost center's name in Workday.
- **Expense approver:** Finance shows afbd67f9619699cfe1988ad9f06c144a, as expected. That is her Workday manager, Avery Carter (E1001), who didn't change in the job change.
- **Other details:** She has no active corporate card and no open expense reports, and no final pay has been requested.

Her job title changed from Software Engineer to Engineering Manager, but her cost center and manager stayed the same. So Finance needs no update for this job change.

Nothing is left unresolved for Finance on this case.
